title: Security post boundaries, factual observation and nonphysical conflict communication
description: Teach respectful boundary statements, behavior-based records, assistance-interface reasoning and accurate post handovers.
purpose: Teach respectful boundary statements, behavior-based records, assistance-interface reasoning and accurate post handovers.

lessons.title: Start here: scope and completion
lessons.body:
This course teaches the document interpretation and planning decisions needed for security post boundaries, factual observation and nonphysical conflict communication. It is intended for the assigned roles listed in the course record. A service catalog label is a starting point for identifying a task; it is not evidence that every employee performs every specialist activity associated with that label. Work through the six lessons, six checks, two fictional worked cases and twenty final questions. The exercises use paper records only and require no equipment operation, live connection or hazardous exposure.

This course is not a security license or legal opinion. It grants no search, detention, force, weapons, law-enforcement, public traffic-control, rescue or clinical authority.

All twenty-six answers must be recorded. Complete every lesson and answer every question correctly, or review and explicitly acknowledge the question-specific remediation. Retain the original selections and first-attempt score alongside corrected answers and the remediation record. Completion documents this knowledge component only. It does not close any unobserved performance requirement or employer authorization.

lessons.title: 1. Read post orders as a boundary of duty
lessons.body:
Security work begins with the actual post and lawful authority, not a uniform or a broad service label. Access coordination, observation, alarm reporting, public traffic control and security-system installation are different duties. This module teaches nonphysical communication and post-order reasoning. It grants no authority to detain, search, use force, carry weapons, direct public traffic or act as law enforcement.

Read the post orders for location, purpose, assigned tasks, prohibited actions, communication contacts and emergency interfaces. Identify who owns access decisions and exceptions. A security worker may be assigned to verify a condition and contact an approver without having authority to invent an exception. A familiar visitor or urgent delivery does not change the assigned decision route. The worker should communicate the actual requirement clearly and preserve a safe interaction.

Legal and credential requirements depend on jurisdiction and duty. Texas DPS's private-security program is an example of a regulator with licensing/registration arrangements; it does not establish every requirement in every jurisdiction. The employer must identify the actual applicable role and current requirements. A general safety course does not create a guard license, and a guard credential does not automatically cover unrelated traffic or technical work.

Create a paper authority table. For each situation, list what the worker observes, what they may decide, what requires an authorized contact and which actions are outside scope. A delivery lacking approval may require a hold and contact, not physical confrontation. A suspected crime may require factual reporting through the designated emergency process, not independent investigation.

Paper exercise: the post order permits checking appointment status and contacting the site host. A supervisor informally asks the worker to search bags. Mark the new requested duty and its unresolved legal/employer authority. Do not infer permission from seniority or the worker's confidence. The actual employer/legal review must establish any such role before training or practice is assigned.

lessons.title: 2. Separate observable behavior from assumptions and bias
lessons.body:
Security observations should describe behavior and conditions rather than diagnose a person's motives, health or character. Someone speaking loudly may be frustrated, unable to hear, distressed or threatening; volume alone does not establish which explanation applies. A reliable report records what was seen or heard, relevant context and uncertainty. Decisions should use the actual post criteria and safety information, not stereotypes about appearance or group membership.

Distinguish facts, interpretations and reported information. I saw the visitor strike the counter is an observation if directly witnessed. The visitor was dangerous is an interpretation. A coworker told me the visitor threatened them is reported information. All may be important, but the record must identify their basis. Quoted words should be accurate and necessary; do not embellish a statement to make the incident sound more serious.

Use a behavior timeline. Record the sequence of relevant events, who was present, what request or information was given and what changed. This helps the responsible team assess escalation and response without relying on a dramatic final label. Do not collect unnecessary personal details or share incident material beyond the approved process. Privacy and evidence handling requirements belong to the actual employer/jurisdiction arrangement.

Paper exercise: replace suspicious-looking man became crazy with a factual account: the visitor raised their voice after being told the host was unavailable, stepped toward the counter and said specified words if actually recorded. Include uncertainty where the learner lacks a direct observation. The exercise does not decide a diagnosis or legal offense.

Observation is not permission to remain exposed. If behavior presents immediate danger, the worker follows the actual emergency/safe-position arrangements and summons appropriate help. Accurate reporting supports response; it does not require approaching a person or delaying protective action to gather a better description.

lessons.title: 3. Use calm, clear verbal boundaries without promising an outcome
lessons.body:
Nonphysical conflict management aims to communicate clearly while preserving safety and role boundaries. Use a calm, respectful tone and short statements about the actual issue. Acknowledge the person's expressed concern without agreeing to an unsupported claim or promising an exception. I understand the delay affects your delivery describes the concern; I guarantee entry in five minutes creates a commitment the worker may not control.

Ask one practical question at a time and allow a response. Competing instructions from several staff can increase confusion. Where the situation and actual plan permit, one assigned communicator can help maintain a clear exchange while others perform their roles. This is a communication principle, not a tactical formation or a guarantee of de-escalation. The worker must not continue talking when the approved response calls for disengagement or emergency assistance.

State a boundary and a legitimate next option. For example: the appointment approval is not confirmed; I can contact the site host through our approved route. Avoid blame, sarcasm, humiliation or arguments about authority. Do not threaten consequences outside the worker's actual role. A lawful site requirement should be explained consistently rather than presented as a personal contest.

Use teach-back for instructions that affect movement or waiting arrangements, when safe and appropriate. Ask the person to confirm the agreed next step in their own words. This identifies misunderstanding without treating them as incapable. Language, hearing or accessibility needs may require the employer's approved assistance arrangement. Raising volume alone is not a substitute for accessible communication.

Paper exercise: a fictional driver says the delay will cost them a job. Draft a response acknowledging the concern, explaining the actual approval status and offering the authorized contact route. Do not promise entry, diagnose the driver or invent a threat. Then identify the conditions under which the worker would follow the local emergency/disengagement process rather than continue the conversation.

Worked wording comparison: you cannot come in because I said so makes the issue personal and gives no useful next step. The approval is not confirmed in the system; I can contact the listed host explains a factual condition and an authorized option. I will get you in shortly adds an unsupported promise and may increase frustration if the host declines. The learner should choose the second statement and explain its limits. It does not guarantee a calm response and does not require continuing an unsafe interaction. If the person reports a language or hearing difficulty, use the approved accessible assistance route rather than repeating the same sentence louder. If the host responds, communicate the actual decision without adding personal conditions. The skill is precise, respectful role-bound communication, not persuasion at any cost.

lessons.title: 4. Plan lone-work, communication and emergency interfaces
lessons.body:
A post can have risk factors related to isolation, time, public contact, money or other actual conditions. OSHA's workplace-violence guidance supports site-specific prevention planning rather than relying only on individual confidence. The employer must assess the actual post and provide appropriate arrangements. A worker should know the relevant communication contacts, assistance process and what to do if the normal channel is unavailable.

Read the communications plan as a practical dependency. Who receives a request for help? What location identifier should be given? Who covers the post if the worker must leave under the approved plan? How are missed check-ins or communication failures handled? The course does not set a universal check-in interval or emergency code. Those details must come from the actual site arrangement and tested capability.

Emergency reporting should be concise and factual. Identify location, nature of the observed concern, people potentially affected and immediate known conditions. State uncertainty. Do not delay an urgent call to complete a perfect written report. Conversely, do not label a routine access discrepancy as a violent emergency simply to get faster approval. Appropriate routing depends on the actual facts and employer plan.

Security can interface with fire, medical, industrial or traffic events. The worker's role may be to summon help, provide information or manage a designated access point under the plan. It is not automatically rescue, firefighting, medical treatment or public traffic direction. Those duties require separate actual training and authority. A uniform does not supply them.

Paper exercise: a lone night post has a radio but no identified responder for radio calls, and the location name differs from the emergency map. Record two readiness gaps: response ownership and location identity. A working radio alone does not establish effective assistance. The employer/site owners must resolve and safely verify the arrangement before it is relied on.

lessons.title: 5. Preserve incident records and useful shift handovers
lessons.body:
An incident record should allow an authorized reviewer to reconstruct the relevant event. Include date/time basis, location, people/roles as needed, direct observations, reported information, actions taken, contacts made and unresolved issues. Separate exact quotations from paraphrases and distinguish estimates from confirmed facts. Do not add a motive or diagnosis because it makes the narrative feel complete.

Record action and result separately. Contacted the host is an action; host approved entry under the actual process is a result only if confirmed. A voicemail is not an approval. A radio transmission is not proof it was received. Closed-loop confirmation is especially useful where the next step depends on a specific authorized decision. Preserve who gave the decision and its scope through the approved record process.

Evidence handling must follow the actual authorized system. Video, photographs and personal data can have privacy, retention and access rules. This course grants no permission to access cameras, copy footage to a personal device, search someone's belongings or publish incident details. A worker can report that relevant evidence may exist and route preservation needs to the responsible role.

A handover should tell the incoming worker the current state, not merely the event's drama. Identify outstanding access decisions, changed site conditions, communication issues, relevant restrictions and responsible contacts. Do not pass unverified rumors as a warning label attached to a person. If an ongoing concern requires special handling, use the employer's approved documented instructions and factual basis.

Paper exercise: the outgoing log says difficult driver, all sorted. The actual record shows host contact pending and the driver still waiting under a designated arrangement. Rewrite the handover to preserve the pending decision and current status. The incoming worker should not infer approval from the word sorted or repeat a character judgment in place of useful operational information.

lessons.title: 6. Assess actual post skills without manufacturing confrontation
lessons.body:
Post-specific competence includes understanding lawful duties, applying actual access criteria, communicating respectfully, recognizing changing conditions and reporting accurately. Credentials where required and practical performance remain separate evidence. A license or registration does not automatically establish skill at this site's systems and post orders. An online conflict-management score does not establish lawful authority for physical intervention.

A safe desk role-play uses fictional visitors and scripted information without threats or surprise physical behavior. Give the learner a post order, an approval discrepancy and a person expressing frustration. Assess whether they explain the actual status, offer an authorized option, avoid unsupported promises and identify when to use the site's assistance route. The actor must not create an uncontrolled confrontation to test bravery.

Practical assessment should be planned by a competent assessor for the actual duties. It can observe approved communication equipment, location reporting, accessible instructions, record completion and post handover under safe conditions. Any separately assigned physical, armed, traffic or emergency role needs its own applicable program and authority. This course teaches none of those techniques.

Feedback should identify the decision or communication behavior, not label the learner's personality. You promised approval you did not control is actionable. You are not assertive enough can encourage unsafe escalation without explaining the task. Retain the original assessment result, coaching and reassessment so that improved performance does not erase the initial limitation.

The final capability handoff should name the post, duties, applicable legal/credential basis, approved orders, practical observations, assessor scope and remaining limitations. Employer/site assignment is a separate decision. Course completion closes only the bounded nonphysical knowledge taught here after correct responses or acknowledged remediation. It cannot issue a security license, authorize searches or detention, qualify weapons/force use or grant public traffic-control powers.

lessons.title: Worked fictional case 1: a frustrated delivery and an unauthorized promise
lessons.body:
Fictional facts: Elm Gate receives a driver whose appointment approval is not confirmed. The driver says the delay may cost them work and speaks loudly. The post order permits appointment checks and host contact. A colleague tells the guard to promise entry shortly and search the driver's bag to show authority. No physical danger is described in the supplied facts.

The learner first identifies actual duty. The guard can check status and contact the authorized host. Neither entry approval nor a search is established by the post order. The colleague's suggestion cannot supply missing legal/employer authority. The learner records the proposed additional duty as outside the established scope rather than trying to perform it confidently.

The response is drafted calmly: acknowledge the driver's stated concern, explain that approval is not confirmed and offer the authorized host-contact route. The learner avoids promising a time or outcome they do not control. They do not diagnose the driver or describe loud speech alone as proof of violence. The actual emergency/disengagement plan remains available if conditions change.

The incident note distinguishes observation from interpretation. It records the expressed concern, raised voice, approval status and contacts made. It does not say the driver was crazy or dangerous without factual basis. A host voicemail is recorded as a contact attempt, not approval.

In the fictional resolution, the responsible host responds through the approved route and the guard records the actual decision and scope. The handover states current status and any remaining conditions. No search, detention or physical confrontation occurs in the exercise.

Final decision: the useful skill is respectful, accurate boundary communication and correct decision routing. Exact residuals are actual jurisdiction/post authority, applicable credentials, site-system instruction and observed practical post performance. A course pass cannot create search powers or turn a colleague's informal request into lawful duty.

lessons.title: Worked fictional case 2: a lone post with an incomplete assistance plan
lessons.body:
Fictional facts: Cedar Security assigns a lone evening post. A radio check produces sound, but no responder is named for assistance calls. The emergency map calls the location West Access while the roster says Yard Two. The outgoing log says difficult visitor, sorted, but a host decision remains pending and the visitor is still waiting.

The learner separates equipment function from response capability. A working radio demonstrates a limited technical observation; it does not establish who will receive and act on a call. The employer/site owners must identify the assistance arrangement and safely verify it. The location-name conflict also needs reconciliation so that a factual emergency report can be understood.

Next, the handover is corrected. The incoming worker needs the pending approval, current waiting arrangement and responsible host contact. The word sorted is misleading because the decision is unresolved. The label difficult visitor is not a useful substitute for behavior and status facts. The learner preserves the original record and supplies a factual clarification rather than inventing a favorable outcome.

The practical assessment is planned safely. A scripted desk exercise can test location reporting, contact routing and handover. It should not stage a surprise confrontation or send the learner into an isolated incident to test confidence. Any real emergency would follow the actual established response process.

In the fictional resolution, the site reconciles location identifiers, names the response roles and provides approved instructions. The learner completes a safe observed communication/handover assessment. The employer separately determines actual assignment readiness and any applicable credential requirements.

Final decision: initial readiness is not established by radio sound or an optimistic log. Exact residuals are an effective assistance interface, correct location identity, post-specific practical capability and actual employer/site authorization. This theory record grants no physical intervention, armed security, medical or public traffic-control authority.

lessons.title: Final assessment and evidence handoff
lessons.body: Complete the twenty final decisions using the methods taught above. For each error, read the explanation and identify the document or reasoning step that would have prevented it. An acknowledgment records reviewed remediation; it does not erase the original answer or imply that a practical task was demonstrated. Your next handoff should name the actual assignment, the documents interpreted, unresolved discrepancies and the person responsible for each decision. Supply the listed vendor evidence and arrange the listed practical assessments separately. Where a credential is legally or contractually required, verify its exact role, method and current scope with acceptable issuing evidence. A course score supplies no new operating, inspection or release authority.
